# @zakkster/lite-binary-reader

Zero-dependency, zero-GC reader for RAW, foreign, or sibling-baked binary
buffers. Point it at an ArrayBuffer (or a typed-array view) plus a caller-
supplied `{ schema, stride, count, byteOffset, littleEndian }` layout and read
fields with NO allocation, at ANY byte offset, with EXPLICIT endianness. Reads
through a DataView, so a field may sit at an odd (unaligned) offset a typed-array
lane cannot address. Single-file ESM, zero runtime dependencies, node:test only.

## Status: 0.3.0 - S4: API sugar (row cursor, readRow, variable-length bytes)

S0 landed the reader and the sibling constructors. S1 hardened the construction
door (BR-01..BR-04). S2 closed the view-window and sibling-shape holes
(BR-05..BR-07). S3 added the shipped ambient types and closed the
detached-ArrayBuffer family:

- `Reader.d.ts`: a hand-written ambient TypeScript surface for the full runtime
  API (`VERSION`, the `T_*` type-code literals, `IS_LITTLE_ENDIAN`, the
  `Field`/`Options`/`Baked`/`Shard` interfaces, the reader class with every
  getter/method/static, and `LiteBinaryReaderError` with a `code` union of all
  10 `R_*` tags). Shipped in the tarball and wired as `package.json` `types`.
- `test/dts-drift.test.js`: a drift gate that reads the TEXT of `Reader.js`,
  `Reader.d.ts`, and `package.json` and asserts three inventories agree -- the
  `R_*` code union, the value-export set, and the version -- each derived by
  regex, never hardcoded, with mutation controls proving the gate has teeth.
- BR-08: a detached (transferred-away) ArrayBuffer, and a view over one, now
  throws a coded `R_BAD_SOURCE` instead of a raw DataView `TypeError`.
- BR-09: a DataView source over a detached buffer now throws a coded
  `R_BAD_SOURCE` -- a DataView's `byteOffset`/`byteLength` getters THROW on a
  detached buffer (a TypedArray's return 0), so the view branch probes the
  underlying buffer for detachment before reading any view getter.

S4 (this release, 0.3.0) adds three additive ergonomic read surfaces on top of
the same zero-GC read path -- the numeric read bodies (getF64..getU8/get) are
byte-identical to 0.2.0, the R_* union stays exactly 10, the type table exactly 8
(both gated by test/dts-drift.test.js), and each new surface has its own 0-B/op
and retained-alloc gate (decisions/0004):

- Row cursor: `seek(row)` (chainable, returns the reader) plus `f64/f32/i32/u32/
  i16/u16/i8/u8(fieldId)` and `val(fieldId)` read at the seeked row without
  re-passing it. The cursor reads inline the same address arithmetic as getX;
  `seek` is unchecked (the same trust model as getX). The stateless row-passing
  getX API is unchanged and stays the recommended form for random access.
- `readRow(row, out)`: fills a caller-owned sink (an Array or any TypedArray)
  indexed by field id, no record object materialized; returns `out`. A sink that
  is null, has no numeric length, or is shorter than fieldCount throws
  `R_BAD_LENGTH` before any write (the door guards the zero-alloc claim: a short
  Array would auto-grow). The loop bounds on fieldCount, not out.length.
- Variable-length `bytes(row, fieldId)`: a 2-arg overload. Mark a schema field
  with `lengthField` naming a sibling field that carries its run length; the
  overload resolves that length per row and returns the borrowed span. Dispatched
  on `len === undefined`; the resolved length flows through the existing
  `R_BAD_LENGTH` / `R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL` doors. An unknown `lengthField` is refused
  at construction with `R_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, a self-reference with `R_BAD_SCHEMA`.
  NO new type code, NO new R_* code -- a variable-length field is an ordinary
  numeric field plus a `lengthField` pointer. The 3-arg `bytes(row,id,len)` is
  unchanged.

## The gap it fills (decisions/0001)

Two sibling packages produce binary, and NEITHER reads arbitrary foreign bytes:

- lite-bake writes an in-memory `{ buffer, stride, count, schema }` in NATIVE
  endianness with no self-describing marker. It cannot read a buffer whose byte
  order differs from the host.
- lite-bake-stream writes a self-describing LBK1 container (its own magic) with
  F64 + U32(string-index) lanes only.

Neither reads a wire protocol, an mmap'd C struct, WASM linear memory, an SoA
column dump, or a record whose fields sit at ODD byte offsets. That is this
module's one job.

## The model (decisions/0001)

A record is `stride` bytes; record `i` starts at `base + i*stride`; each field
has a byte `offset` within the record and a `type` code. A read is one
`DataView.getX(base + row*stride + off, littleEndian)` -- no allocation, no
parsing, no object materialized. Resolve a field NAME to an integer id ONCE with
`field(name)` outside the loop, then index by that id in the hot loop.

## Type codes (decisions/0001)

Byte-for-byte lite-bake's `Types` table, so a lite-bake schema drops in unchanged:

- T_F32 = 0, T_F64 = 1, T_I32 = 2, T_I16 = 3, T_I8 = 4, T_U32 = 5, T_U16 = 6,
  T_U8 = 7. Widths in bytes: [4, 8, 4, 2, 1, 4, 2, 1].

LBK1's `lane_kind` is a DIFFERENT table that collides by value (only F64 is
shared); `fromLBK1Shard` TRANSLATES it (1=F64, 2=F32, 3=U32, 4=U8) so a single
ambiguous integer never crosses the boundary. An LBK1 U32 cell is a string-table
INDEX; read raw it returns that index number (string resolution stays in
lite-bake-stream).

## The construction door (decisions/0002, 0003)

All validation and any allocation happen at construction or on the throw path;
the read hot path is unchecked for speed. The door fails closed and every error
carries a coded `R_*` tag on `error.code`:

- The source is coerced to an OWNED buffer. An ArrayBuffer is used zero-copy. A
  FULL-SPAN zero-offset typed view unwraps to its buffer zero-copy. ANY other
  view -- a nonzero-byteOffset view OR a zero-offset PARTIAL view -- is COPIED to
  its own window so a derived or explicit count can never exceed the bytes the
  view owns (BR-07).
- A detached backing store (BR-08 / BR-09) is refused with `R_BAD_SOURCE` before
  `new DataView`. Detection: an `ArrayBuffer.prototype.detached` probe on Node
  21+, and a guarded `DataView` construction on the `node>=18` floor (a live
  zero-length buffer constructs fine; a detached one throws). A legitimately
  zero-length buffer is NOT misclassified as detached.
- `byteOffset` past the buffer end throws `R_BAD_OFFSET` before a count is
  derived (BR-01); a NaN/fractional byteOffset is caught, not swallowed by
  `|| 0` (BR-03); a non-integer type throws `R_BAD_TYPE` (BR-02); a duplicate
  field name throws `R_DUPLICATE_FIELD` (BR-04); a stride smaller than the
  largest field end throws `R_BAD_STRIDE`; `count*stride` past the buffer throws
  `R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL`.

## Read codes (R_*), exactly 10

- R_BAD_SOURCE      source is not an ArrayBuffer/view, or its buffer is detached
- R_BAD_SCHEMA      schema is not a non-empty array of field descriptors
- R_BAD_TYPE        a field.type is not an integer in 0..7
- R_BAD_OFFSET      a field.offset or byteOffset is not a coherent non-negative
                    integer, or byteOffset falls past the end of the buffer
- R_BAD_STRIDE      stride is not a positive integer, or < the largest field end
- R_BAD_COUNT       count is not a non-negative integer
- R_BAD_LENGTH      bytes() len is not a non-negative integer
- R_DUPLICATE_FIELD two schema fields share a name (a silent shadow is refused)
- R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL declared count*stride (+base) exceeds the buffer, or a
                    bytes() span reads past the buffer
- R_UNKNOWN_FIELD   field(name) was asked for a name not in the schema

## API (0.3.0)

Named exports from `@zakkster/lite-binary-reader`:

- VERSION: '0.3.0'
- IS_LITTLE_ENDIAN: boolean (host byte order, detected once)
- T_F32=0, T_F64=1, T_I32=2, T_I16=3, T_I8=4, T_U32=5, T_U16=6, T_U8=7
- LiteBinaryReaderError: Error subclass; `.code` carries the R_* tag
- LiteBinaryReader: the reader class (also the default export)

Constructor:

- new LiteBinaryReader(source, { schema, stride?, count?, littleEndian?,
  byteOffset? })
  - source: ArrayBuffer or any ArrayBufferView (TypedArray or DataView).
  - schema: non-empty Array of { name, type, offset, lengthField? }. name is a
    string or number; type is a T_* code (0..7); offset is a non-negative integer;
    optional lengthField (S4) names a sibling field carrying this field's run
    length, enabling the 2-arg bytes(row, fieldId) overload.
  - stride: bytes per record; defaults to the tightly-packed minimum (the
    largest field end).
  - count: record count; defaults to floor((byteLength - byteOffset) / stride).
  - littleEndian: read byte order; default true (the sane wire default).
  - byteOffset: where the record region starts inside the buffer; default 0.

Introspection (cold):

- get count / get stride / get fieldCount / get littleEndian / get buffer
- field(name) -> integer id (throws R_UNKNOWN_FIELD). Call ONCE, outside the loop.
- typeOf(fieldId) -> the field's type code
- offsetOf(fieldId) -> the field's byte offset within a record

Read hot path (zero-alloc; row in [0,count), fieldId a valid id, UNCHECKED):

- getF64/getF32/getI32/getU32/getI16/getU16/getI8/getU8(row, fieldId) -> number.
  One method per type keeps each call site monomorphic and branch-free.
- get(row, fieldId) -> number. Generic; dispatches on the stored type code (one
  branch per read). Use a typed getX in a tight loop; use get when the type is
  data-driven.

Row cursor (S4; zero-alloc; sequential-scan sugar over the same read path):

- seek(row) -> the reader (chainable). Sets the cursor; UNCHECKED (same trust
  model as getX). Only seek moves the cursor.
- f64/f32/i32/u32/i16/u16/i8/u8(fieldId) -> number. Read fieldId at the seeked
  row; each is the matching getX body with the cursor row substituted.
- val(fieldId) -> number. Generic cursor read; dispatches on the stored type code.
- The row-passing getX API stays stateless and is the recommended form for random
  access; both read the same bytes.

Row fill (S4; zero-alloc into a caller-owned sink):

- readRow(row, out) -> out. Fills out[i] with field i of `row` for i in
  [0,fieldCount); `out` is an Array or any TypedArray. No record object is
  materialized. A sink that is null, has no numeric length, or is shorter than
  fieldCount throws R_BAD_LENGTH before any write (guards the zero-alloc claim: a
  short Array would auto-grow). The loop bounds on fieldCount, not out.length.

Escape hatch (allocates ONE small view wrapper -- not zero-GC, not for the frame
hot path):

- bytes(row, fieldId, len) -> a BORROWED Uint8Array view over `len` raw bytes at
  the field position. It aliases the buffer; copy what you keep. A bad len throws
  R_BAD_LENGTH; a span past the buffer throws R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.
- bytes(row, fieldId) -> the same, with `len` read per row from a sibling field
  (S4). Mark the field with `lengthField` naming the sibling that carries the run
  length. Dispatched on len === undefined; the resolved length flows through the
  same R_BAD_LENGTH / R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL doors. Calling it on a field with no
  lengthField throws R_BAD_LENGTH. NO new type code, NO new R_* code.

Sibling cooperation (cold constructors):

- LiteBinaryReader.fromBaked(baked, options?) -> reader over a lite-bake
  `{ buffer, stride, count, schema }`. The schema drops in unchanged; read as
  NATIVE endianness (lite-bake writes native with no marker). A null/malformed
  argument throws a coded R_BAD_SOURCE / R_BAD_SCHEMA (BR-06).
- LiteBinaryReader.fromLBK1Shard(shard, options?) -> reader over ONE carved LBK1
  shard `{ bytes, rowStride, fields:[{name,laneKind,offsetInRow}] }` from
  lite-bake-stream. Translates lane_kind -> our type code; read little-endian
  (LBK1 is little-endian by spec). A null/fieldless argument throws a coded
  R_BAD_SOURCE / R_BAD_SCHEMA (BR-06).

## Zero-GC posture (suite CLAUDE.md)

Zero allocation on the read hot path: getX / get / the cursor reads (seek +
f64..u8 / val) / readRow into a reused sink / the row address arithmetic allocate
nothing, each with its own 0-B/op and retained-alloc gate. Every allocation lives
at the construction door or on the throw path. `bytes()` is the one intentional
exception (a Uint8Array view wrapper) and is documented as such. The torture gate
(`node --expose-gc test/torture.mjs`, @zakkster/lite-leak +
@zakkster/lite-gc-profiler) proves 0 B/op and 0 retained bytes across the read
loop and prints exactly `ok`; a `LBR_TORTURE_BREAK=1` control injects a retained
allocation and the gate rejects it (a gate that cannot fail is decorative).

## Testing

- npm test        -- 60 node:test cases (contract + boundary + drift)
- npm run torture -- @zakkster/lite-leak + lite-gc-profiler: 0 B/op, prints `ok`
- npm run torture:controls -- the door/coherence controls
- npm run verify  -- test + torture + controls, the publish gate

## Composability

- @zakkster/lite-bake: read its baked `{ buffer, stride, count, schema }` output
  with `fromBaked` -- the type table is shared, so the schema drops in unchanged.
- @zakkster/lite-bake-stream: read one carved LBK1 shard with `fromLBK1Shard`.
- Any raw/foreign source: a wire frame, an mmap'd struct, WASM linear memory, an
  SoA column dump -- pass the ArrayBuffer (or view) with an explicit layout.
